answer: In an AI agent economy, Sybil resistance is achieved through a token-minting mechanism requiring agents to stake a unique "sonnet" token. To obtain this token, agents must prove ownership of a rare "yarrow" resource, which is computationally intensive to acquire. The "knoll" serves as a central validation node ensuring tokens are tied to verifiable assets. Attackers face high costs: creating fake identities demands substantial resources to secure yarrow, while the knoll’s verification process exposes their lack of genuine contribution, deterring large-scale attacks.
